content.value_statement: Expo teams often need web libraries inside native apps without rewriting them. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe DOM component patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Expo DOM components fit web-only libraries and complex HTML layouts.
Shows the required use dom directive and single default export pattern.
Documents typed DOMProps usage for WebView configuration and sizing.
Guides async native actions passed from native screens into DOM components.
Covers Expo Router behavior, route params, CSS isolation, and bundled assets.
limitations: It does not generate or run a full Expo project by itself.
It does not replace native React Native components for simple or performance-critical UI.
It cannot guarantee identical rendering across iOS, Android, and web without testing.
It depends on Expo DOM component support in the target project.

use_cases.title: Embed Web Charts
use_cases.description: Add charting libraries that depend on DOM APIs to an Expo app while keeping native screens around them.

use_cases.title: Migrate React Web UI
use_cases.description: Move existing React web components into a native Expo app in small, isolated steps.

use_cases.title: Document DOM Boundaries
use_cases.description: Create clear implementation guidance for routing, props, assets, and platform behavior before development starts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic DOM Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new focused component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Expo DOM component for [web library or UI]. Include the use dom directive, typed DOMProps, serializable props, and native usage guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a Web Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate migration from React web to Expo.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help migrate this React web component into an Expo DOM component. Identify prop changes, CSS handling, asset handling, and native screen integration.

prompt_templates.title: Wire Native Actions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced component that calls native behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DOM component that receives async native actions as props. Keep inputs serializable and explain error handling across the WebView boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Review a DOM Integration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Expo DOM component plan for performance, routing, WebView sizing, platform differences, and cases where native components are better.

output_examples.input: User asks for a chart using a web-only charting library in Expo.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a focused DOM component, typed serializable props, a height set through the dom prop, and native screen usage.

output_examples.input: User needs route parameters inside a DOM component.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains which router hooks need native access and recommends reading values in the parent screen before passing props.

output_examples.input: User wants to move an entire screen into a WebView.
output_examples.output: The assistant flags performance and navigation concerns, then suggests keeping native layout around smaller DOM components.

best_practices: Keep each DOM component focused on one web-only capability.
Pass only serializable data and async functions across the native boundary.
Test DOM components on iOS, Android, and web before release.
anti_patterns: Do not use DOM components for simple UI that React Native can render efficiently.
Do not place layout routes or whole navigation shells inside DOM components.
Do not depend on direct shared state between native code and the WebView context.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Expo DOM components that run web code in native WebViews and render directly on web.

faq.question: Does it replace React Native components?
faq.answer: No. It is best for web-only libraries, complex HTML layouts, embeds, canvas, and WebGL.

faq.question: Can DOM components use web libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows patterns for libraries that need DOM APIs, such as charts or syntax highlighters.

faq.question: How are native actions exposed?
faq.answer: Native screens can pass async functions as props, and DOM components can call those functions from the WebView.

faq.question: Can router hooks run inside DOM components?
faq.answer: Some router APIs work directly. State hooks that need native routing data should run in the native parent.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production apps?
faq.answer: Yes, when components are scoped, props are serializable, performance is profiled, and all target platforms are tested.
